assignments.package_label_en: Stories of the Righteous and the Great Light
assignments.reason: The totality of holiness (כלליות הקדשה) is the essential nature of both השגחה and ארץ ישראל in this Torah. The Rebbe states: 'השגחה, הינו שיצא מטבעיות, שזה בחינת כלליות הקדשה' and 'כי ארץ ישראל הוא כלליות הקדשה שבכל הקדושות.' This concept IS holiness in its totality — the transcendent dimension that enables distinguishing light from darkness. Its essential nature is the all-encompassing holy awareness that belongs to Package 1's domain of expanded luminous consciousness. Both השגחה and ארץ ישראל (already added to Package 1 via additions) are identified as bechinas of כלליות הקדשה, making this node a natural member of the same good/holiness cluster.

assignments.package_label_en: Stories of the Righteous and the Great Light
assignments.reason: This node — the act of telling stories of the righteous — is essentially the same concept as מעשיות של צדיקים (already in Package 1) but phrased as the active verb form ('to tell'). Its essential nature IS the domain of holy stories, the Great Light, expanded consciousness. The node_id 'לספר מעשיות של צדיקים' is the practical/verbal expression of 'מעשיות של צדיקים.' The Torah explicitly identifies stories of the righteous as 'בחינת מחין דגדלות' and 'בחינת המאור הגדול' — the core identity of Package 1. While it produces effects (purifying thought, saving from troubles), the concept itself IS the holiness-of-stories domain.

assignments.node_id: שספורי מעשיות מצדיקים. הינו ממה שארע להם
assignments.node_text: שֶׁסִּפּוּרֵי מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת מִצַּדִּיקִים. הַיְנוּ מִמַּה שֶּׁאֵרַע לָהֶם
assignments.package_label_en: Stories of the Righteous and the Great Light
assignments.reason: This is a longer-form alias of the core Package 1 concept: 'stories of what happened to the righteous.' The Torah opens with: 'דע שספורי מעשיות מצדיקים, הינו ממה שארע להם, הוא דבר גדול מאד, ועל ידי זה נטהר מחשבתו.' The essential nature of this node is identical to ספורי מעשיות של צדיקים and מעשיות של צדיקים — all are expressions of the same holy-stories/great-light domain. The phrase 'הינו ממה שארע להם' simply specifies that the stories concern events that occurred to them, but does not change the conceptual domain.

connected_to: שספורי מעשיות מצדיקים. הינו ממה שארע להם
assignments.package_label_en: Stories of the Righteous and the Great Light
assignments.reason: Purification of thought (נטהר מחשבתו) is the essential outcome that defines the entire teaching. But more than an outcome, it IS the state of expanded, luminous consciousness — the world of thought (עולם המחשבה) purified and elevated. The Torah says: 'ועל ידי זה מטהר מחשבתו ממחשבות רעות, שהם נמשכין ממחין דקטנות' — purified thought is the state of being freed from constricted mind (Package 2's evil domain) and restored to expanded mind (Package 1). The Rebbe further says: 'ואזי נטהר מחשבתו, ויכול לעלות אל עולם המחשבה, שזה נקרא עליית העולמות' — purified thought = ascending to the World of Thought = the elevation of consciousness. This is the positive/holy pole: thought aligned with the Great Light. Its essential nature is holy, expanded awareness — Package 1.

assignments.package_label_en: Constricted Mind and the Forces of Judgment
assignments.reason: Being saved from troubles (ניצול מצרות) is essentially a concept defined by what it describes: צרות (troubles). The Torah states: 'גם ניצול מצרות. כי בלבול הדעת הוא בחינת מחין דקטנות, ומזה באין צרות, כי מחין דקטנות הם בחינת דינין.' The troubles themselves ARE dinin, ARE constricted mind — they belong to the evil domain of Package 2. While the SAVING from troubles is a positive result, the node 'נצול מצרות' is defined by the צרות it addresses. Just as in Torah #1 where 'הכנעת היצר הרע' (subjugation of the evil inclination) was assigned to Package 3 because it describes what happens TO the evil force, here 'being saved from troubles' describes the resolution of Package 2's evil domain. The concept's essential nature is the trouble-domain being overcome, and צרות is already identified as belonging to Package 2 (via additions).

assignments.node_id: שיוכל להדמות אליו יתברך להבדיל בין אור וחשך
assignments.node_text: שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִדַּמּוֹת אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין אוֹר וְחֹשֶׁךְ
assignments.package_label_en: Stories of the Righteous and the Great Light
assignments.reason: The ability to resemble God by distinguishing between light and darkness is the master capacity of this Torah — it is the prerequisite for telling stories of the righteous (the Torah's opening statement: 'אי אפשר לספר מעשיות של צדיקים כי אם מי שיכול להדמות עצמו להשם יתברך, דהינו שיכול להבדיל בין אור וחשך'). Its essential nature is the capacity for holy discernment — seeing with the luminous expanded awareness that belongs to Package 1. This is not a neutral faculty; it is explicitly aligned with holiness ('כמו השם יתברך כביכול'). The concept IS the God-like faculty of knowing light from darkness, which is the very definition of expanded holy consciousness (מחין דגדלות = the Great Light that illuminates the difference). It belongs to Package 1 as the foundational capacity underlying all the package's other concepts.

assignments.package_label_en: Stories of the Righteous and the Great Light
assignments.reason: Transcending nature (שיצא מטבעיות) is identified by the Rebbe as identical to השגחה and כלליות הקדשה: 'על ידי השגחה, הינו שיצא מטבעיות, שזה בחינת כלליות הקדשה.' The word 'הינו' (that is) makes this an explicit identity statement: השגחה = exiting the natural = totality of holiness. Its essential nature is the transcendence of the natural/material dimension into the supernatural/holy dimension — the same luminous, expanded awareness that characterizes Package 1. Exiting nature is not a neutral concept here; it is the very definition of entering holiness ('כלליות הקדשה'). This concept belongs in Package 1 alongside השגחה (already added), ארץ ישראל (already added), and כלליות הקדשה (assigned above).
